question_text:
The diffusion coefficients for nickel in iron are given at two temperatures, as follows:

\begin{tabular}{cc}
\hline$T(\mathrm{~K})$ & $D\left(\mathrm{~m}^2 / \mathrm{s}\right)$ \\
\hline 1473 & $2.2 \times 10^{-15}$ \\
1673 & $4.8 \times 10^{-14}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

(a) Determine the values of $D_{0}$ and the activation energy $Q_{d}$.
(b) What is the magnitude of $D$ at $1300^{\circ} \mathrm{C}(1573 \mathrm{~K})$ ?

Give your answer as a tuple ($D_{0}$, $Q_{d}$, D at $1300^{\circ} \mathrm{C}(1573 \mathrm{~K})The units of each required answer are (m^2/s, J/mol, m^2/s), respectively.
response:
Using the Arrhenius relation $D = D_0 \exp(-Q_d/RT)$ and taking the ratio of the two data points to eliminate $D_0$:

$$\ln\!\left(\frac{D_2}{D_1}\right) = -\frac{Q_d}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_2}-\frac{1}{T_1}\right)$$

$$Q_d = -\frac{R\ln(D_2/D_1)}{(1/T_2-1/T_1)} \approx 3.156\times10^{5}\ \text{J/mol}$$

Then $D_0 = D_1\exp(Q_d/RT_1) \approx 3.48\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$, and at $1573\ \text{K}$:

$$D = D_0\exp(-Q_d/RT) \approx 1.13\times10^{-14}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$$

$$\boxed{(3.48\times10^{-4},\ 3.156\times10^{5},\ 1.13\times10^{-14})}$$
